**There is a deliberately encoded message: "SATURN HAS RINGS OF ICE".**

### What carries the information (explicitly derivable)

1. **Building heights encode letters (A=1 … Z=26).** The skyline has 19 buildings, each exactly 20 px wide on a 30 px pitch, with tops at y = 90, 270, 80, 70, 100, 140, 200, 270, 90, 100, 190, 140, 210, 90, 130, 220, 190, 250, 230 and a common base at y = 279. Every building is an exact multiple of 10 px tall, and each 10 px band holds one row of two lit windows, so the number of floors is (280 − top)/10. Floor counts left to right:

   `19 1 20 21 18 14 | 8 1 19 | 18 9 14 7 19 | 15 6 | 9 3 5`
   `S  A T  U  R  N  | H A S  | R  I N  G S  | O  F | I C E`

2. **Trees mark the word breaks.** The four identical trees sit in the only widened gaps in the skyline (x≈210, 330, 510, 600), i.e. after buildings 6, 9, 14 and 16 — splitting the string into word lengths 6/3/5/2/3: SATURN · HAS · RINGS · OF · ICE.

3. **Checked and ruled out as carriers:** all 420 windows are lit with the identical colour (no on/off pattern); the sky is a clean per-row gradient with zero stray pixels; the moon is a featureless disc; the ground strip segments merely mirror the building gaps; the PNG has no text chunks. A full connected-component census found exactly 31 elements (7 stars, moon, 19 buildings with the one antenna, 4 trees) and nothing else.

### Unexplained / decorative elements
The 7 stars (identical 2×2 dots at seemingly arbitrary positions), the moon, and the red-tipped antenna on the tallest building all look purely decorative — I could not derive any encoding from them, and I'm not claiming one.

### Confidence
Very high (~98%). The mapping is simple and mechanical, every one of the 19 heights falls in the 1–26 range, and the output is a grammatical, meaningful English sentence with word breaks that coincide exactly with the tree positions — essentially impossible by chance.
